title: Structure à l'infini des Mg,ν [pages 1 à 90, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Section 9 opens the 'MDT-structure': the groupoid structure of the modular Teichmüller groupoids, here in the transcendental (complex-analytic) setting, together with the 'morphismes de généralisation'. Grothendieck now works with the analytic moduli stacks M_{g,ν}^an and their compactifications, and drops the superscript 'an'.

For each MD-graph G (a modular dual graph, i.e. what is now called a stable graph: vertices α with genera g_α and legs/half-edges) there is a complex 'multiplicité modulaire' (orbifold or stack) M_G. This is the stratum of the boundary of the Deligne–Mumford compactification M̄_{g,ν} of dual-graph type G. Up to the finite group Γ_G = Aut G, M_G is the product ∏_α M_{g_α, I_α}.

Grothendieck takes the fundamental groupoid ΠM_G. This is a 'big' category whose objects are all points. He states the principle that, in the constructions to come, one may replace ΠM_G by an equivalent groupoid with a finite object set, provided the replacement is Γ_G-equivariant: Γ_G must act and the equivalence must commute with that action. In modern terms, one passes to a full subgroupoid on a finite Γ_G-stable set of base points meeting every component. The many-base-point fundamental groupoid then has a finite presentation.

The next page completes the thought:
- ΠM_G has connected pieces whose π1 is ∏_α of the Teichmüller (mapping class) groups T_{g_α,ν_α}.
- The orbifold (M_G, Γ_G) has a fundamental group that is an extension of Γ_G by that product (formula 96).
- He then announces two kinds of morphisms between the groupoids attached to different MD-graphs: 'specialization' maps, coming from morphisms of MD-graphs, and 'generalization' maps, coming from edge contraction. The previous page uses edge contraction to show that orderings define points of a common component.

The overall aim is the Teichmüller tower of the Esquisse: a functor from the category of stable graphs (with contractions and automorphisms) to finitely presented groupoids. This is the object on which Gal(Q̄/Q), and hence Grothendieck–Teichmüller, should act.
errors: No real error. One subtlety is that strict Γ_G-equivariance of the equivalence requires the finite base-point set to be Γ_G-stable. Γ_G is finite and acts on the points of M_G, so such a set exists (take finitely many Γ_G-orbits meeting every component); the claim is fine. For the stack, base points at fixed loci of the action must be handled in the orbifold sense, which Grothendieck implicitly does via the orbifold fundamental group on the next page.

ideas.what: Fundamental groupoid of the boundary stratum M_G attached to a stable (MD-) graph G, with the action of Aut G
ideas.modern_name: Fundamental groupoid of a boundary stratum of M̄_{g,n}; orbifold π1 as an extension of Aut(G) by a product of mapping class groups
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (Esquisse 1984) programmatically; worked out by Hatcher–Lochak–Schneps, Nakamura, Bakalov–Kirillov (c. 1997–2000)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (Teichmüller tower, §§2–3), in outline only

ideas.what: Replace the 'big' fundamental groupoid by an equivalent groupoid with finitely many objects, compatibly with the finite symmetry group
ideas.modern_name: Full subgroupoid on a finite Γ-stable set of base points (equivariant skeleton); 'groupoïde fondamental en plusieurs points base'
ideas.where_published: SGA1 (fundamental groupoid), Esquisse d'un programme (choice of base points)

ideas.what: Organising the groupoids over all MD-graphs, with specialization/generalization (edge-contraction) morphisms, into one structure (the 'MDT-structure')
ideas.modern_name: Modular operad (in groupoids) indexed by stable graphs; Teichmüller groupoid tower
ideas.usually_credited_to: Getzler–Kapranov (modular operads, 1998); Bakalov–Kirillov / Moore–Seiberg (Teichmüller tower / Lego); HLS
ideas.where_published: Esquisse gives the 'tour de Teichmüller' idea, but not this graph-indexed formalism

missed.claim: Grothendieck sets up a functor from MD-graphs (stable graphs with automorphisms and contractions) to Aut(G)-equivariant fundamental groupoids of strata. This is essentially a groupoid-valued modular operad over stable graphs, predating Getzler–Kapranov's formalism. On this page, however, it is only announced.
missed.quote: il est en effet licite de remplacer un groupoïde tel que ΠM_G par un groupoïde équivalent, pourvu que le groupe Γ_G = Aut G opère, et que l'équivalence commute à l'action de ce groupe
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is historical evidence that the stable-graph / modular-operad organisation of the Teichmüller tower, now standard in Grothendieck–Teichmüller theory, was explicitly in Grothendieck's notes, including attention to equivariance under graph automorphisms.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a set-up page: the definitions and the base-point/equivariance principle are standard and the Teichmüller tower is in the Esquisse. The only mild interest is the explicit graph-indexed, Aut(G)-equivariant framework anticipating modular operads.
transcription_corrections: 'que le moins nous allons voir pouvons le remplacer' should read roughly 'comme nous allons voir, nous pouvons le remplacer'.
The insertion over 'catégorie' (struck) is 'groupoïde'. The word read as '{+ensemble[?]+}' above it is probably a struck 'analogue' or similar, not 'ensemble'.

Title: insertion above the line reads approximately 'groupoïdes modulaires des'; the main line reads 'La structure groupoïdale des Teichmüller multiplicités modulaires'. The intended sense is the groupoid (Teichmüller) structure on the modular multiplicities.

'pourvu que [l'équivalence] des catégories ... [le groupe]': 'le groupe' is struck at the start of the line before (94); the sense is 'pourvu que le groupe Γ_G = Aut G opère, et que l'équivalence commute à l'action de ce groupe'.
